commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries, with an optional port suffix that
is required to match exactly when present.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling:
The defect is split between the producer and the consumer of the bracketed-IPv6 "port suffix".

Commit 9b4334a (knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals) owns the validator, knownhost_ipv6_part(). Its edit relaxes the acceptance rule for bracketed entries: instead of requiring ']' to be followed by ':<digits>', the port suffix becomes optional, so a stored name like "[2001:db8::1]" now parses successfully and yields an EMPTY suffix (a pointer to the terminating NUL of the heap-allocated node->name, which knownhost_add() sizes exactly strlen(name)+1). On its own this is harmless: the suffix is still compared with strcmp(), and an empty suffix simply never matches ":22", so behavior stays memory-safe (probe is clean on a tree with only this edit).

Commit 6605f79 (tidy-up: miscellaneous) owns the consumer, knownhost_plain_match(). Its edit replaces the plain strcmp() of the two suffixes with a "compare ports numerically" helper for bracketed entries; the helper unconditionally skips the leading ':' (host++/known++) before scanning digits. Under the ORIGINAL validator this assumption holds (a bracketed entry always yields ":<digits>" or is rejected outright), so this edit alone is also memory-safe (probe is clean on a tree with only this edit).

Only the composition is faulty: with the relaxed validator, a bracketed entry can now reach knownhost_port_equal() with an empty suffix, and the unconditional ':'-skip steps one byte past the end of the exact-size node->name allocation; the following *known digit test is a 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) reached from libssh2_knownhost_readline() + libssh2_knownhost_checkp() with a regular OpenSSH known_hosts line.

A correct fix is necessarily non-local: reverting or bounding only the consumer keeps the (now documented) portless-bracketed acceptance in the validator working, and reverting only the validator leaves the numeric-port comparison intact but changes the accepted-entry behavior back; either single-commit revert removes the crash, but understanding why requires reading both diffs - the consumer's ':'-skip is only unsafe because a DIFFERENT commit widened the set of suffixes the validator can emit. There is no single-commit diff that both preserves each commit's stated maintenance intent and fixes the read without reasoning across the two commits.

pocs.entry_point: libssh2_init + libssh2_session_init + libssh2_knownhost_init + libssh2_knownhost_readline + libssh2_knownhost_checkp (public <libssh2.h> API)
